newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea Metals - Won rally spurs base metals buying.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Metals - Won rally spurs base metals buying.

text.p: South Korean demand for base metals was picking up this week after the won's recent sharp gains against the dollar, traders said on Thursday.
The won's rise should boost demand from local buyers who have reduced inventories to save on carrying costs during the local currency's recent long slump.
"Now it's time to buy metals," a trader with a major trading house said.
The won ended higher at 854.90 won against the dollar for the third consecutive day on Thursday, supported by active dollar-selling intervention by the central Bank of Korea.
The won had traded at around 869.00 a week ago.
Aluminium import premiums were firm on recent strong demand from Japan and European countries, traders said.
Premiums for the second quarter shipment were expected to rise to $85-$90 a tonne CIF Pusan over London Metal Exchange (LME) cash prices, compared with $65-$70 for the first quarter.
Aluminium import premiums for spot delivery have remained unchanged at $90 a tonne CIF Pusan, traders said.
Domestic Aluminium prices fell to 1.48 million won a tonne from 1.50 million won a week ago on the currency's sharp gains, while copper prices were unchanged at 2.279 million won.
Zinc and lead prices were also unchanged at 1.079 million won and 728,000 won a tonne respectively.
